approach:
Root cause: after a squash the host's commit is not a descendant of the job's landed commit, and `resync_tip` (crates/athena-core/src/land.rs:218) fixes that by `git.replay`, which rebuilds every commit after the landed one under new ids. The branch therefore leaves its remote copy's history and a plain push is refused.

Change:
1. `resync_tip` builds a merge commit instead. The tree is `git.merge_tree(landed, head, merged)`, so main's changes beyond the landed job are carried in and a later edit of the landed job's lines does not conflict. The commit is `git.commit_tree(tree, [head, merged], message, sign)`. The first parent is the branch head and the second is the host's commit, so every old commit stays an ancestor. The message ends with the line `Resynced-Landed: <landed sha>`. The key has no `Athena-` prefix, because D133 and the trailer-stop tests forbid `Athena-` lines after C0. The no-op cases (merged already an ancestor of head; landed not on head) stay, and a conflict is an error that moves nothing.
2. `resync_onto_merge` keeps `reset_keep(tip)`, which here is a forward move that keeps local edits. Its messages and docs change from "rebuilt" to "merged".
3. A merge keeps already-squashed landing commits in the branch history. The next pull request's range `remote_base..head` (`pr_commits`, land.rs:267, and `check_pr_head`, pr_check.rs:47) would list them again, plus the merge commit. That merge commit is judged against its first parent and fails as `GovernedChange` when main moved by other governed content. To prevent this, a new helper `pr_range` in land.rs excludes every landed sha named by a `Resynced-Landed` line on a merge in the range (`rev-list --reverse base..head ^landed…`) and drops those merge commits. Everything reachable from a squashed commit is in main, so the exclusion is exact; unlanded stack commits below it (job B in the existing test) are kept. `pr_commits` and `check_pr_head` both call it.
4. A new `Athena::push_working_branch(ui)` in land.rs pushes the current branch to `origin` with `Git::push_branch` (plain, no force, no `push_if_remote_at`). It prints a line on success. A failure, a detached HEAD or a missing remote prints `warning: …` and never errors, so the landing stays landed. `after_merge` (gh/landing.rs:959) calls it after the resync, which covers `athena land --pr` and the drain's `PrLander`, because both go through `Athena::land_pr`. `RealSteps::land` (drain.rs:4450) calls it after any lander returns `Landed`. The drain test then drives that seam with the existing `Lander` double, which skips `after_merge`. When the remote copy already holds head the push is silent, so the real drain, which reaches both call sites, does not push twice.
5. The cutover fixture (test_support.rs:559) and `trailer_stop.rs:131` call `resync_onto_merge` on a checkout that is `main` itself. Attribution walks main's first-parent line from C0 (attribution.rs:386), and a merge would put C0 off that line. Both fixtures move to the host commit with `reset_keep(c0)` instead, which gives the same tree and history as the old replay did (nothing followed the landed commit). The new tests cover the working-branch merge.
6. Docs: update the `resync_onto_merge`, `resync_tip` and `after_merge` comments; rewrite the resync paragraph of docs/design/native-pr-landing.md §5.2a; add D168 to docs/decisions.md (appended, superseding D88's tradeoff); add the CHANGELOG entry. No config files change.

Commit-shape table (a landing rule changes: the PR range):
| Shape | `pr_range` outcome |
|---|---|
| Job landing commit not yet squashed | kept, `JobLanding` |
| Records-only commit | kept, `RecordsOnly` |
| Owner-path commit | kept, `RecordsOnly` where the rules exclude the path (unchanged) |
| Intervention commit | kept, `DeclaredIntervention` |
| Retry-after-block landing (a later commit adds `outcome-landed.json`) | kept, `JobLanding` (unchanged) |
| Resync merge (parents: head, host commit; has `Resynced-Landed`) | dropped from the range |
| The landed commit named by a resync merge, and all its ancestors | excluded (already in main by the squash) |
| Unlanded stack commit below a landed one | excluded if an ancestor of the landed commit (the squash holds it); kept if not |
| Commit after the merge | kept and classified as before |
| A merge without the line | kept and judged as before |

The realistic-branch fixture holds an intervention, a records-only commit, job A's landing, job B's landing, the resync merge for A, and job C's landing. Expected range: B, C. It differs from the real repository in using small files and fake records, and in having no host.

decisions.choice: Make the merge tree with `merge_tree(base = landed, ours = head, theirs = merged)` and write it with `commit_tree` (parents head, then merged), then move the branch with `reset_keep`.
decisions.reason: A plain `git merge` uses the real merge base, which conflicts whenever a later job edits the landed job's lines. The existing test `after_a_squash_the_branch_is_rebuilt…` has exactly that case. With the landed commit as base, only main's changes beyond the landed job come in, which is what the replay produced. It needs no new Git API: `merge_tree`, `commit_tree` and `reset_keep` exist and keep local edits, and signing follows `signs_commits`.

rejected.why: It conflicts on later edits of the landed lines, can leave a half-done merge in the work tree, and bypasses the signing and keep-edits behavior of the existing helpers.
Out of scope and rejected by the request; it treats the symptom.

decisions.choice: Mark the merge with a trailer-form line `Resynced-Landed: <landed sha>`, and exclude those landed shas from the pull-request range in `pr_range`.
decisions.reason: A squash never makes the landed commit reachable from main, so a retained history re-lists already-landed jobs in the next landing intent and landing record. It also lists the merge commit, which fails `classify_pre_merge` when main moved by other governed content. Excluding the ancestors of the recorded landed commit is exact, because the squash holds everything the pull request carried. The key avoids the `Athena-` prefix (D133, `has_athena_line` in trailer_stop.rs).

rejected.option: Do nothing in `pr_commits` and accept re-listed jobs
rejected.why: It would duplicate job landings and make the landing intent fail when main moved by other governed content.

rejected.option: Teach the gate's `classify_pre_merge` to skip merges whose other parent is on main
rejected.why: It would weaken the gate (an arbitrary tree could ride a merge), and the gate is outside the deliverables.

rejected.option: Cut each job's pull request from main (per-job-main-landing.md)
rejected.why: A separate proposal (D167), not part of this request.

decisions.choice: Push from two call sites: `after_merge` (for `land --pr` and `PrLander`) and `RealSteps::land` (for the drain), through one helper that does nothing when the remote already holds head.
decisions.reason: The drain's tests use the `Lander` double, which never reaches `after_merge`. A drain-level push is the only one a drain test can observe through an existing seam. The `land --pr` command has no seam below `GhCli`, so its push sits in `after_merge`, which `after_merge_tests.rs` already calls directly. The helper's silent no-op on an up-to-date remote avoids a second push in the real drain.

rejected.why: `commands::land` is a binary function that needs the real `gh`, so no test could show the push.
The drain test could not observe it without putting the push logic in the test double.

decisions.choice: A failed push is a warning line and the landing stays landed; the push is plain via `push_branch`, never forced.
decisions.reason: The merge is already done on the host. The request asks for a plain push, and a refused push (for example a branch whose remote rules reject merge commits) must not undo a landing.

rejected.option: Return the push error from `after_merge` or `RealSteps::land`
rejected.why: It would turn a completed landing into a failure and trigger a drain retry.

decisions.choice: Move the two fixtures that resync a checkout that is `main` itself to `reset_keep(c0)` instead of `resync_onto_merge`.
decisions.reason: Attribution and the history check read main's first-parent line from C0. A merge on a branch named `main` would put C0 off that line and fail the fixture's `--attribution` checks. The old replay produced exactly C0 here (nothing followed the landed commit), so `reset_keep` is the same result. Merge-shape coverage lives in the new tests.

rejected.why: `athena check --attribution` on the fixture's local main would report the cutover commit as not on main's first-parent line.

decisions.reason: athena-git's own tests exercise `replay`; removing it is a separate clean-up outside the request.

rejected.why: Wider than the request, and its tests would have to go.

It reads `current_branch` and `head` (a detached HEAD or no commit gives a warning line); it asks `ls-remote` through `GitRemote::remote_head` (a remote already at head returns true silently); otherwise it calls `self.git.push_branch("origin", &branch, &head)` and prints `pushed <branch> to origin at <short>` or `warning: could not push <branch> to origin: <reason>; the landing stands`. It never returns an error.

risks.risk: The merge keeps all landed commits in the branch history, so `plan_rebase`/`rebase_job_branch` (landing.rs:665, 761) would replay them. Both are exported but not called in production, as a search of crates/ shows (only tests call them).
risks.mitigation: Not wired into production, so no change now. D168 and the changelog note that if it is wired later it must use `pr_range`'s exclusion.

risks.risk: The history check (athena-gate) judges the merge by its first parent and could report it when main carried other governed content.
risks.mitigation: The merge is dropped from the pull-request range, so landing intents and `check_pr_head` are safe. The gate is left as it is and the User question names the follow-up. The tests cover the case where main moved only by the squash.

risks.risk: A pull-request range that names the landed sha but the sha is missing from the object store would break `rev-list`.
risks.mitigation: `pr_range` skips a `Resynced-Landed` value that `commit_exists` does not find (the line is only ever written from a commit that was on the branch).

risks.risk: The push is refused or `origin` is unreachable.
risks.mitigation: A warning line, not an error; the landing and the local resync stand, and the next landing pushes the whole append-only history with a plain push.

risks.risk: Existing tests assume a rewritten branch (text needle, linear shape, `main == C0`).
risks.mitigation: The dependents list names each; the full `cargo test --locked` and the per-crate runs in criterion 6 cover the rest.

risks.risk: The first landing after this change pushes a branch whose remote copy was force-pushed by hand, so the plain push may be refused once.
risks.mitigation: A warning line states the reason; the maintainer reconciles by hand once, after which pushes are plain.
